versions.content:
# Paralegal practice (firm policy)

- Deadlines: send Docketing a written request with the triggering document, the rule and your count. Docketing
  enters it; the responsible attorney confirms. Never rely only on the system's default count.
- Paralegals don't give legal advice, set fees, accept or decline clients, sign discovery, or make privilege or
  strategy decisions (NALA Canon 1; ABA Model Guidelines for paralegal services, Guideline 3). Say you are a
  paralegal at the start of any call with a client or prospective client (NALA Canon 5).
- New prospective clients: take name, adverse parties and a brief description only, then send to Conflicts and
  the partner. No discussion of the merits until conflicts clear and an attorney accepts the matter.
- CM/ECF: you may file with an attorney's login only for a document that attorney has signed and authorized you
  to file (N.D. Ill. General Order 16-0020).
- Material from the other side that appears privileged or inadvertently produced: stop reviewing, sequester it in
  Relativity, and tell the supervising attorney at once (Model Rule 4.4(b); FRCP 26(b)(5)(B); the protective
  order's paragraph 14).
- Confidential client material goes out only through the firm's secure share (Kiteworks), not personal email.

# Lakeshore Packaging Co.: outside counsel billing guidelines (2026)

1. Time in tenths of an hour (0.1). No minimum charges.
2. No block billing: each task has its own entry and time.
3. Not billable: clerical or administrative tasks (scheduling, copying, scanning, filing documents in the
   firm's own system, booking rooms or vendors) at any rate; internal conferences unless the purpose is stated;
   more than one timekeeper at a deposition without approval.
4. Approved rates: partner $640, senior associate $495, associate $380, paralegal $195.
5. Pre-bills reviewed by the billing attorney before the invoice is sent on the 10th.
